transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-03-26
- Start: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Tanya (Redwood CSM), Daniel (Lucent HoML), Aisha (Procurement), Raj (Security), Leah (Legal)

Summary (auto): Procurement kickoff to review MSA/DPA, pricing, SLAs, and pilot. Action items captured.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can get started. i'm Samira, AE on the account, with Marcus our SE, and Tanya from onboarding. how's everyone today?
[00:08] Daniel: Good thanks, Samira. appreciate you making time. we have Aisha and Raj and Leah on the call for legal and security side.
[00:15] Aisha: Hi all, thanks. we want to focus on the MSA redlines and pricing, plus timeline to get a pilot running.
[00:23] Samira: absolutely; quick agenda - 1) MSA/DPA redlines you flagged, 2) SLA and dedicated capacity pricing, 3) security questions re: KMS and audit logs, 4) next steps. sound okay?
[00:33] Raj: yep, that's fine. first off, encryption and key management - we need to know if keys can be customer-managed, bring-your-own-key, and HSM support.
[00:42] Marcus: yeah so Redwood Private and Dedicated both offer KMS integrations; for Hosted we do offer envelope encryption and a KMS option for enterprise tenants. HSM is supported for Private/On-prem deployments. i can send the tech spec after. there was a note in the doc about HSM vs cloud KMS, that may have been mis-typed in the earlier PDF.
[01:00] Leah: on the DPA - we flagged data retention and deletion clauses; we need explicit deletion certs and audit trail for any derivatives. currently the clause is somewhat generic.
[01:12] Tanya: understood - we typically provide audit logs and retention settings per account; deletion certs are available for Private/Dedicated. for Hosted we can do data retention windows and a documented deletion workflow, though customers sometimes request an added attestation.
[01:27] Daniel: got it. on SLAs, our internal SRE org wants 99.9 availability and p95 latency targets for inference under our expected load. what do you usually guarantee for Dedicated?
[01:38] Marcus: for Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime with options up to 99.95 depending on the reserved config. latency SLOs are more workload dependent; we publish verified profiles for models and can commit to p95 ranges in the MSA for specific endpoints as part of the pilot and runbook. we also offer fallbacks to other model variants in the routing policy to preserve availability.
[01:56] Aisha: pricing - we need committed pricing for a 12-month commitment; can you provide examples of how committed tiers discount vs on-demand? also interested in overage terms.
[02:06] Samira: yes - we'll send a pricing spreadsheet with tiered discounts; for example 12-month commit at X tokens/month gets ~22% off on-demand, plus reserved GPU credits for Dedicated and predictable throughput. overage billing is prorated at the committed rate until you hit the next tier, but we can be flexible on enterprise deals.
[02:25] Raj: about compliance: SOC2 and ISO certifications - we saw SOC2 Type II on the site. do you have a SOC2 report or pen test attestations to share?
[02:35] Tanya: we can share the SOC2 report under NDA and our latest penetration test summary. i will upload the security pack to the shared doc link.
[02:44] Leah: also need specifics on sub-processors and data residency - we have EU customers so data residency matters.
[02:51] Marcus: for Dedicated and Private, data never leaves your VPC / on-prem. for Hosted we offer region isolation and can sign data residency addendums; sub-processors are listed in the security pack. we'll include region options and any constraints in the runbook.
[03:08] Daniel: ok on the pilot: we want a small, scoped pilot to validate latency and accuracy. can you run the pilot in our dev account or do we need to provide sample logs?
[03:18] Marcus: best path is to run an initial performance run in our dev environment with your sample prompts and we can reproduce in your dev account for benchmarking. for Dedicated throughput tests we'll need a short window of traffic and test harness - we usually run a 48-hour soak to get p95 numbers.
[03:35] Aisha: timeline wise, procurement wants to sign MSA/DPA within two weeks if redlines are reasonable. is that feasible?
[03:42] Samira: yes, that's feasible. we'll send tracked MSA/DPA with our standard language and note any terms that usually require legal review, like indemnity caps and data handling. If Lucent returns redlines we'll coordinate with our legal and aim for a signature within the 2-week window.
[03:56] Leah: one specific ask - can you add a clause to explicitly state that derivatives created from customer-provided data are subject to deletion on request?
[04:05] Marcus: i can't commit legal language, but operationally we can include delete operations for KV cache and model outputs for Private/Dedicated, and for Hosted we'll document the retention/deletion procedure and provide attestations. we'll log this as an item for legal.
[04:18] Daniel: for the pilot success criteria - we want: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), 2) throughput of ~50 concurrent requests at 100 QPS sustained, 3) no data exfil concerns and signed DPA.
[04:33] Marcus: sounds reasonable. quick note - 300ms p95 depends on model choice and quantization; if you pick a smaller open model we can achieve lower latency per GPU. we'll include model recommendations and quantization options in the bench plan.
[04:47] Samira: we'll include model/cost tradeoffs in the pricing sheet. also i'll put together two purchase options: hosted with data residency + contractual clauses, or Dedicated reserved capacity with a 12-month commit.
[04:58] Aisha: on invoicing and PO - we need to know billing cadence and whether you support net-30 and PO numbers on invoices.
[05:06] Tanya: we support invoice terms net-30 and net-45 for enterprise, and can accept PO numbers. we'll include the billing terms in the commercial sheet.
[05:13] Raj: one more security ask - can you provide audit log retention durations and whether logs include per-request prompt text? we need to control prompt visibility for sensitive data.
[05:23] Marcus: audit logs can be configured - by default we log metadata and request IDs; request payload logging can be toggled, and for Private/Dedicated you can disable payload retention. we'll document the fields and retention windows in the security pack.
[05:35] Samira: great - i think we're aligned on next steps. Tanya will own docs and SOC2 upload, Marcus owns the runbook and bench plan, i'll own pricing and legal coordination.
[05:46] Daniel: thanks. expecting the redlined MSA/DPA and pricing by end of week so procurement can review.
[05:53] Aisha: yep, we'll prioritize review.
[06:00] Samira: perfect thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and set the SE deep dive for early april.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Samira to send pricing spreadsheet and example committed tiers (due 2026-03-29)
- Marcus to share Dedicated onboarding and bench runbook (due 2026-04-02)
- Tanya to upload SOC2 report under NDA and coordinate MSA/DPA redlines (due 2026-04-01)
- Schedule SE deep dive for benchmark run in Lucent dev account (propose 2026-04-06)

References / Links mentioned in call:
- Redwood MSA & DPA (will send tracked)
- Pricing spreadsheet (to be attached)
- Dedicated onboarding playbook (SE runbook)
- Security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary)

End of transcript.
